race_context: Northwest Allen County Schools (NACS) serves northwest Allen County north of Fort Wayne, with one high school; a third middle school, Willow Creek, was scheduled to open in August 2026 {jg_nonres26}. Wayne Barker is superintendent {jg_ref25}{jg_nonres26}. A current districtwide enrollment figure could not be confirmed from a fetched source.

The board has five members who serve four-year terms {jg22_prev}. The district lists Liz Hathaway (president), Kristi Schlatter (vice president), Darren Vogt (secretary), Erica Jamison and Liz Chaffee {nacs_board}. Jamison and Chaffee were elected in 2024 {jg24_res}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 3, held by Schlatter, and the at-large seats held by Hathaway and Vogt, who were the top two finishers for two at-large seats in 2022 {jg22_res}{jg_fil26}. The Allen County Election Board's list, as reported by The Journal Gazette, shows Schlatter (District 3), Vogt (at large, Republican) and Hathaway (at large, Republican) as the only NACS candidates, all incumbents {jg_party26}.

Seat count: the state list shows the at-large race (labeled District 4) as vote for 1 with two candidates {in_list}. Both at-large incumbents' terms end in 2026, and The Journal Gazette describes both as unchallenged incumbents {jg_party26}{jg22_res}, which indicates two at-large seats are being filled. If so, all three NACS seats on the ballot are uncontested.
Filing: newcomer Matthew Cohee also filed for an at-large seat in June 2026 {jg_fil26}, but he is not on the October candidate list {jg_party26} or the state list {in_list}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Allen County school board candidates could declare a party; Hathaway and Vogt filed as Republicans and Schlatter left the box blank {jg_fil26}{jg_party26}. School board races are excluded from straight-party voting {jg_party26}.

Operating referendum (Nov. 4, 2025): voters rejected an eight-year operating referendum of up to $0.2787 per $100 of assessed value (about $12.2 million a year), 3,952 to 3,368, according to final unofficial results {jg_ref25}{wboi_ref25}. The money would have gone mainly to staff pay, instructional support, the career and technical education (CTE) facility, and safety and well-being staffing {wboi_ref25}. Barker said NACS receives about $8 million a year less than the state average and that the district would move forward within its existing budget {jg_ref25}{wboi_ref25}.

Budget and SEA 1 (2025–2026): for 2026, NACS prepared a budget of nearly $126 million and estimated a $2.7 million property tax cap loss, about $1.6 million of it in the operations fund; the CFO said the plan to absorb this was $11 million in general obligation bonds over two years for technology and transportation {jg_bud25}. A third-party summary of the Aug. 17, 2026 board meeting reports a financial presentation on SEA 1 and says the board decided not to make a $38 million capital investment in a swim-trials pool project {govly_aug26}.

Enrollment and school choice (2026): in April 2026, Barker put enrollment about 300 students below projections, which officials attributed to vouchers, housing trends and falling birth rates; the board approved open enrollment for non-residents and changes to the preschool {wpta_enr26}. The board agreed to accept up to 340 non-resident students in fall 2026 and had received 129 transfer requests by May 4 {jg_nonres26}.

Facilities: the board redrew middle school boundaries in January 2026 ahead of Willow Creek Middle School's scheduled August 2026 opening, and limited 2026 middle school transfers to Willow Creek {jg_nonres26}.

Forums: no 2026 NACS candidate forum or questionnaire was found. Because the seats appear uncontested, the most recent issue statements from these candidates come from 2022 campaign coverage {jg22_prev}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, unopposed for reelection in District 3; listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}{nacs_board}{jg_fil26}.
background: In 2022 she was listed as a former teacher and homemaker {jg22_prev}.
She is a NACS graduate whose children have graduated from Carroll High School or attend NACS {jg22_prev}.
She was appointed to the board in 2017, ran unopposed in 2018, and won District 3 in 2022 with 53.2% of the vote {jg22_prev}{jg22_res}.

items: In 2022 she said the most pressing need was managing the district's population growth while maintaining educational excellence {jg22_prev}.

on_incumbent: In 2022 she said six years on the board had taught her the value of long-term planning that gives the board options and sets up future district leaders {jg22_prev}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large member and board secretary, elected in 2022; listed as Republican. He lost the May 2026 Republican primary for state Senate District 15 by 14 votes {in_list}{nacs_board}{jg22_res}{ipm_recount2}.
background: He is a staffer to U.S. Sen. Jim Banks {ipm_recount1}{ipm_recount2}.
In 2022 he was described as a local business owner and NACS parent with 12 years on the Allen County Council, six as president, and a seat on the Allen County Redevelopment Commission {jg22_prev}.
He won the second of two at-large seats in 2022 with 21.7% of the vote, according to unofficial results {jg22_res}.

He ran in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary for state Senate District 15 against Sen. Liz Brown. Certified tallies gave Brown 5,241 votes to his 5,227 {ipm_recount2}. He asked for a recount on May 19 and withdrew the request in July 2026, saying the vote totals would not change enough to affect the outcome {ipm_recount1}{ipm_recount2}{fwb_recount}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for reelection to an at-large seat as a Republican while the Senate primary recount was pending {jg_fil26}{fwb_recount}.
Listed on the state ballot list as Republican {in_list}.

items: In 2022 he said schools should focus on basics such as reading and writing {jg22_prev}{jg22_res}.
In 2022 he supported redrawing NACS board voting districts to match population growth, and said the district might be better served by seven board members instead of five {jg22_prev}.

on_incumbent: As a 2022 candidate, he said of the board he had watched in recent years that "They really needed some leadership" {jg22_prev}. No 2026 statement on the board's record was found.
endorsements_finance: In 2022 he was endorsed by then-Congressman Jim Banks; the Purple for Parents of Indiana group and a "Conservative NACS School Board Candidates 2022" Facebook page also backed him {jg22_prev}{jg22_res}.

In his 2026 state Senate campaign, state filings show $90,000 from Attorney General Todd Rokita's campaign fund and $35,000 from Sen. Banks's campaign account {ipm_recount2}. No school board campaign finance report for 2026 was found.
gaps: No 2026 school board website, questionnaire or forum statements were found; his school-board issue statements are from 2022.
His votes on the 2025 referendum, SEA 1 budget actions and 2026 open enrollment were not found in fetched sources.
A search snippet (unverified) says he took office on the board Jan. 1, 2023.
No 2026 school board campaign finance report was found.
